nc-mecklenburg-2026-district-attorney-me.name: Spencer Merriweather
nc-mecklenburg-2026-district-attorney-me.bio: Mecklenburg County District Attorney since 2017; previously an Assistant District Attorney for eleven years.

positions.stance: Has championed a Family Justice Center so survivors of sexual assault, child violence and domestic violence can get services "under one roof."
"Reducing illegal gun possession will certainly help us keep some families from losing their loved ones."
"Those who suffer from addiction, whose only crime is drug possession, will be given ample opportunity to receive treatment."
"Civilians and law enforcement must build and maintain a criminal justice system that deserves public confidence and trust."

nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-singh.name: Mona Singh
nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-singh.bio: Technology leader and innovator with over 130 U.S. patents and a community advocate and grassroots organizer.

positions.stance: Will advocate for public schools and community colleges, "including well-paid teachers and well-equipped classrooms."
Wants Wake County to adopt "smart, responsible technologies" while prioritizing the protection of residents' privacy.
Will use data-driven insights to make county services such as housing, healthcare, public safety and transit more seamless and accessible.

nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-kushn.name: Christine Kushner
nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-kushn.bio: Former Wake County Board of Education member and chair (elected 2011); serves on the Wake County Health and Human Services Board.

positions.stance: Supports preserving existing housing, adding mixed-income and affordable developments, and linking expanded transit such as Bus Rapid Transit to housing.
"I am a fierce advocate for public education"; wants commissioners committed to improving Wake schools with well-paid staff and educators.
Supports better access to public health and social services, including foster care improvements, maternal and child health, and expanded substance use treatment.
Says budgets and policies "should reflect our shared values for open government and transparency," with diverse voices heard in decisions.

nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-harto.name: Gary Dale Hartong
nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-harto.bio: Professional engineer and President of The Wooten Company, a North Carolina civil and environmental engineering firm.

positions.stance: Wake County should ensure roads, water, sewer, parks, buildings and broadband keep pace with growth through strategic, data-driven capital planning.
Existing school facilities should be modernized and new schools designed to reduce long-term operations and maintenance costs.
Supports local businesses and working with the State and municipalities to build technology, life sciences, manufacturing and healthcare hubs.
Wake County should "re-examine its revenue sources, lower the tax burden where possible, and refocus spending on core services."

nc-wake-2026-sheriff-blackwell-kenneth.name: Kenny Blackwell
nc-wake-2026-sheriff-blackwell-kenneth.bio: Retired law enforcement officer who served as a Wake County deputy, a U.S. Marshal, and a State Capitol Police investigator.

positions.stance: Lists "Reduce Response Times" among his priorities as sheriff.
Lists "Rescue Victims of Human Trafficking" among his priorities as sheriff.
Lists a "Fentanyl and Opioid Crackdown" among his priorities as sheriff.
Lists "Expand Mental Health Services" among his priorities as sheriff.
Lists "Increase Salaries for Deputies and Detention Officers" among his priorities as sheriff.

nc-wake-2026-sheriff-rowe-willie.name: Willie Rowe
nc-wake-2026-sheriff-rowe-willie.bio: Wake County Sheriff; 30-year veteran of the Wake County Sheriff's Office who retired as a Major in 2013, and a U.S. Army veteran.

positions.stance: Will increase officer presence and community engagement and take "a proactive, data-driven, and people-centered approach to enforcement."
Aims to restore public trust in the Sheriff's Office and establish "open and honest communication with the community at large."
Will recruit, vet, train and equip qualified staff, fill current vacancies, and maintain sufficient staffing to improve morale.

nc-wake-2026-district-attorney-nickel-ge.name: Wiley Nickel
nc-wake-2026-district-attorney-nickel-ge.bio: Attorney and former North Carolina state senator and U.S. Congressman.

positions.stance: Prioritizes gun violence, drug trafficking, violent crime and property theft while supporting drug diversion programs for nonviolent offenders.
Supports giving departments resources to train, staff and retain officers, and "disagrees with those in his party who want to defund the police."
Working to expand victim support services and specialized prosecutor training for domestic violence, sexual assault and child abuse cases; supports tougher penalties for repeat offenders.
Pushing state and local leaders to fix Wake County's understaffed District Attorney's office.
Says corruption cases are handled "by the facts and the law, no matter who's involved or what party they belong to."
Will "continue to focus on keeping our county moving forward with new jobs and opportunities for individuals and families."
Will invest federal infrastructure funding in projects such as roads, bridges and parks "that will benefit all residents."

ma-suffolk-2026-da-hayden-kevin.name: Kevin R. Hayden
ma-suffolk-2026-da-hayden-kevin.bio: Suffolk County District Attorney; former prosecutor in the District Attorney's office and defense attorney.

positions.stance: Committed to working with law enforcement and communities against gun trafficking, including the Boston FIRST program and a Firearm Rapid Indictment Program.
Created a Community Engagement/Strategic Partnerships Division and supports grant funding for community violence and substance use prevention programs.
Believes those struggling with opioid addiction "in most cases, need treatment, not incarceration"; expanded the Services over Sentences program.
Created the Suffolk Restorative Justice program, a voluntary process bringing non-violent offenders, victims and community members together to address harms.

ma-suffolk-2026-register-of-probate-ever.name: Stephanie L. Everett
ma-suffolk-2026-register-of-probate-ever.bio: Register of Probate for Suffolk County since August 2023.

in-marion-2026-prosecutor-mears-ryan.name: Ryan Mears
in-marion-2026-prosecutor-mears-ryan.bio: Marion County Prosecutor who has served nearly his entire career in the Marion County Prosecutor's Office.

positions.stance: His office expanded the Special Crimes Unit and Criminal Charging Division to "hold violent offenders accountable in the courtroom."
"The Marion County Prosecutor's Office isn't going to waste one resource prosecuting pregnant people, doctors and nurses who seek or provide abortion care."
His office no longer prosecutes marijuana cases involving one ounce or less.
Established Indiana's first Conviction Integrity Unit to prevent, identify and remedy wrongful convictions.
Established Second Chance Workshops, Project Valid and other initiatives to restore driver's licenses for Marion County residents.

in-marion-2026-prosecutor-foust-philip.name: Philip Foust
in-marion-2026-prosecutor-foust-philip.bio: Former Marion County deputy prosecutor and current Clerk-Treasurer for the Town of Speedway.

positions.stance: Wants "clear standards, real consequences, and a juvenile system the public can actually see" for teen offenders.
Would refocus on enforcing the law and seeking justice for victims, starting with a first-100-days review of the worst repeat offenders' cases.
Says public safety "cannot succeed when the prosecutor alienates police, surrounding prosecutors, and the Statehouse."

in-marion-2026-sheriff-williams-kelvis.name: Kelvis T. Williams
in-marion-2026-sheriff-williams-kelvis.bio: Retired Indiana State Police major and Executive Officer of the Marion County Sheriff's Office.

md-baltimore-city-2026-sa-bates-ivan.name: Ivan J. Bates
md-baltimore-city-2026-sa-bates-ivan.bio: Baltimore City State's Attorney since 2023; former prosecutor and defense attorney.

positions.stance: Prosecution plan pillar: "Focusing on Prosecuting Illegal Gun Possessors, Users, & Traffickers."
Prosecution plan pillar: "Protecting Victims & Witnesses."
Prosecution plan pillar: "Rebuilding Strong Interagency Collaboration with Public Safety Partners."
Supports "Alternatives to Incarceration & Community Courts for Low Level Offenders."
Supports juvenile prosecution that "Prioritizes Public Safety & Rehabilitation Through Accountability."

md-baltimore-city-2026-sheriff-tapp-harp.name: Sabrina Tapp-Harper
md-baltimore-city-2026-sheriff-tapp-harp.bio: Retired Baltimore City Police Department major and retired Assistant Sheriff of the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office.

md-montgomery-2026-exec-jawando-will.name: Will Jawando
md-montgomery-2026-exec-jawando-will.bio: Civil rights lawyer and Montgomery County Council member who worked in the Obama White House.

positions.stance: "Fully fund our schools, shrink class sizes, expand Pre-K, and ensure every child gets a world-class education regardless of zip code."
"Produce affordable housing, preserve what we have, and protect renters from displacement."
"Protect our green spaces, accelerate clean energy, and ensure climate action reaches every community equitably."
Build "a transparent, accountable government that works for people, not powerful interests" with real ethics enforcement and community input.
Make the county "a national model for inclusion, with fully funded special education and services."

md-montgomery-2026-exec-wells-esther.name: Esther Wells
md-montgomery-2026-exec-wells-esther.bio: Certified Public Accountant who has served as President of the Montgomery County Taxpayers League.

positions.stance: Would restore the $692 homeowner property tax credit, reverse the recent 4.7% property tax rate hike, and limit assessment increases.
Will "lead with measurable goals, fiscal stewardship, and transparent government—centered on affordability, accountability and private sector growth."
Would fully staff the police department, restore School Resource Officers in schools, and strengthen juvenile justice laws for repeat offenders.
Wants "Student First" school budgets, an independent Inspector General for MCPS, and school resource officers in every high school.
Would attract corporate headquarters and high-paying jobs to broaden the tax base and block or weaken all-electric energy mandates.

md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-elric.name: Marc Elrich
md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-elric.bio: Longtime Montgomery County community and tenant organizer.

md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-goldb.name: Scott Evan Goldberg
md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-goldb.bio: Small business owner and Montgomery County Public Schools substitute teacher.

positions.stance: Would upgrade to seven full-time, paid Board of Education positions with dedicated staff and increase funding for students with special needs.
Would brand the county as a leader in hospitality, healthcare, high tech and craft brewing to attract jobs and companies.
Would make dense housing near transit easier to build, reform the voucher system, and build mixed-income social housing on county-owned land.
"We will not tolerate antisemitism in any shape, form, or expression"; wants more county funding to keep all faiths safe from violence.
Says "the climate crisis is the lens through which all public policy should be viewed."

md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-sayle.name: Laurie-Anne Sayles
md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-sayle.bio: Montgomery County Councilmember At-Large and Chair of the Council's Health and Human Services Committee.

positions.stance: Will continue "driving innovation, strengthening educator pipelines, and expanding hands-on learning" from cradle to career.
Supports affordable housing funding, rent stabilization and "Ban the Box," and connecting housing with health and human services.
Supports local agriculture, farm-to-food bank partnerships and a resilient food system to eliminate health disparities.
Prioritizes affordability and economic growth "without overburdening taxpayers," including workforce development and support for small businesses.
Will advance climate solutions through "smarter transportation systems, stronger public transit, and expanded clean energy investments."

md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-silve.name: Karla Silvestre
md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-silve.bio: Montgomery County Council member and Fiscal Management Committee chair; former Board of Education president and longtime Montgomery College staff member.

positions.stance: Will streamline permitting, lower child care costs, expand apprenticeships, and help federal workers connect to new jobs.
Supports more housing near transit, "missing middle" housing, accessory dwelling units, and mixed-income and deeply affordable housing.
Will protect sustainable school funding, demand transparent budgets, and strengthen pathways from MCPS to college and careers.
Will "stand firmly for due process, family unity," and access to services without fear, including legal aid for immigrant families.
Will expand programs that help seniors safely age in place and support family caregivers.

md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-wells.name: Sherwin Wells
md-montgomery-2026-council-atlarge-wells.bio: U.S. Army veteran with over 25 years of experience in financial services, real estate and mortgage lending.

positions.stance: Will push the county to work with neighboring jurisdictions to reopen White's Ferry as soon as possible.
Committed to an open-door policy so residents and business owners can easily reach their council member.
Supports regular performance reviews and measurable benchmarks for elected officials and county departments.
Supports investing in first responders and improving emergency preparedness and disaster response planning.
Wants more funding for shelters, transitional housing and supportive services to reduce homelessness.
